finding.reproduction: Before the source fix, the actual native PostgreSQL canonical consumer executed the registered story handler and persisted the domain terminal row, then the registry refreshed public status while worker_jobs was still running. That refresh overwrote the just-written terminal projection and assertDomainExecutionSucceeded failed with status=running for success, failure, and missing-domain-row cases.
finding.repair: runVerticalDramaStoryJob now checks tenant, user, and series from the canonical job context against the loaded domain record before status writes, execution, assurance work, or notifications. It returns its persisted terminal domain record, null when the row is missing, the owner mismatches, or the durable story-generation fence is lost. The canonical registry evaluates that worker-local outcome after its lease assertion; public getVerticalDramaStoryJobStatus still refreshes from canonical worker_jobs. Canonical success output carries the domain result so later public refreshes retain the result payload.
